eventsConfig._about: Which economic events the Calendar shows (D23: legitimately important events only; D24: every market-moving report and every scheduled Fed-official appearance; D95: useful data only). Read and checked by server/lib/calendar/config.js (validateEvents, filterEvents). An event is kept when one rule of its feed matches: the event's kind is the feed's kind, its title matches the rule's title pattern (a regular expression, case-insensitive), and every structured match the rule lists holds (impacts: Forex Factory's rating; fedTypes: the Fed file's event type; auctionTypes: TreasuryDirect's type; exclude: a Treasury field value that rules the event out). Every other event is dropped and counted per feed per day. When the Fed or Treasury and Forex Factory list the same event (FOMC items, a Board member's appearance, the Beige Book, a coupon auction), merge.js shows it once, at the official time. A kept event carries the rule's emphasis: normal, or low for an item D26 keeps but shows small.

forexfactory.comment: Adam's own Forex Factory settings (D24): US (USD) events only, which the parser already applies; high, medium and low impact; all event types; the grey non-economic ones (holidays) are hidden. Market closures come from the NYSE calendar instead.

keep.what: Every USD event rated high (red), medium (orange) or low (yellow)
keep.basis: D24 (Adam's Forex Factory filter) and D26 (nothing on the list is cut; low impact is shown de-emphasised by its yellow rating)

fed.comment: The Federal Reserve calendar carries FOMC events, Board members' appearances, the Beige Book and about twenty statistical releases. Only the first three, the Monetary Policy Report and the weekly balance sheet are kept. The releases G.17 (industrial production) and G.19 (consumer credit) are left out because Forex Factory lists the same reports with an impact rating; keeping both would show each twice. Commercial paper, H.6, H.8, H.10, H.15, G.5, G.20, Z.1 and the like are left out (D95). Staff testimony (a division director) is left out: D24 names Fed officials, and staff are not policymakers.

keep.what: Every event the Fed files as type FOMC: meeting (rate decision), statement, press conference and minutes
keep.basis: D24 (FOMC meetings, rate decisions, minutes and press conferences)

keep.what: An FOMC meeting, statement, press conference or minutes the Fed files under another type (the 2021-05 minutes were type Board)
keep.title: ^FOMC (Meeting|Statement|Press Conference|Minutes)\b
keep.basis: D24, as for the fomc rule

keep.what: Any speech, discussion, lecture, panel, testimony or other appearance by the Chair, a Vice Chair or a Governor, whatever type the Fed files it under
keep.title: \b(Chair|Chairman|Governor)\b
keep.basis: D24 (every scheduled appearance by any Fed official: "anytime a Fed member farts I want to know about it"); regional Fed presidents come from Forex Factory

keep.title: ^Beige Book\b
keep.basis: D26 (Fed is on the list sent to Adam) and the archived calendar-sources note (ARCHIVE.md: Fed JSON for FOMC, Beige Book and Board speeches)

keep.what: The twice-yearly Monetary Policy Report to Congress
keep.title: ^Monetary Policy Report\b
keep.basis: D24: it is the written half of the Chair's twice-yearly testimony

keep.what: The Fed's weekly balance sheet (H.4.1, Factors Affecting Reserve Balances)
keep.title: ^H\.4\.1\b
keep.basis: D26: the Fed weekly balance sheet is shown de-emphasised, not removed (lead, 2026-10-27: lowest importance)

treasury.comment: Treasury coupon auctions only: every fixed-rate note and bond (2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20 and 30 years), reopenings included. TreasuryDirect names a reopening by its remaining term (a reopened 10-year is "9-Year 10-Month Note"), so the title is not read: TreasuryDirect's own type (Note or Bond) and flags decide. Bills and cash-management bills (weekly, routine), floating-rate notes and TIPS are left out that way, since an FRN or TIPS is also security type Note.

keep.what: Fixed-rate Treasury note and bond auctions, new issues and reopenings
keep.basis: D26 (bonds are on the list sent to Adam) and D23 (legitimately important only): the coupon auctions are the ones the bond market trades on; the lead's brief names 2, 5, 10 and 30 years at minimum
